sentence: A 53-year-old man presented with intense pain in the left iliac fossa without other associated symptoms.
He denied the existence of fever.
He did not report regular home treatment or personal or family history of interest.
The physical examination revealed a slight overweight and painful palpation at the level of the left iliac fossa, along with abdominal guarding.
Bowel sounds and the rest of the examination were normal.
The general analysis revealed a GGT of 88 U/l, ferritin of 297.11 ng/ml and CRP of 7 mg/dl.

Given the persistence and intensity of the pain, as well as to confirm the suspected diagnosis, a CT scan of the abdomen was performed, which revealed the existence of sigmoid diverticulosis without signs of diverticulitis.

In an upper section of the abdomen, an inflammation of the fat adjacent to the descending colon was observed, which corresponded to an epiploic appendix, probably in the context of acute appendagitis secondary to torsion of the same.

The patient was diagnosed with "appendagitis" or "epiploic appendagitis" and received conservative treatment with oral anti-inflammatories for 7 days, with a progressive improvement of symptoms and without complications appearing.
The use of antibiotics or hospital admission was not necessary.
